# hermes-lcm v0.23.1

Stable privacy-only release for hosted summary embeddings. Runtime bytes are unchanged from
`v0.23.1-rc1`; this promotion changes release metadata only and makes no database schema change.

## Highlights

- Every supported cloud summary-vector dispatch fails closed unless sensitive-pattern
  handling is enabled, nonempty, recognized, current, and residual-clean (#330).
- Provider input uses pattern-only placeholders that reveal no raw value, length, bytes, or
  secret-derived digest. Durable messages, summaries, FTS rows, and payloads are unchanged.
- Vector identity includes `privacy:v1:<active-pattern-hash>`; policy drift requires a fresh
  warmup before cloud dispatch.
- Complete and truncated private-key blocks are conservatively replaced before transport.

## Validation

- The immutable RC passed detached release validation and privacy-hostile regressions.
- Independent Eva donor clones passed fake-capture and real Voyage summary-vector backfills,
  15-tool acceptance, restart/replay checks, and copied-state rollback.
- Eva passed exact-RC live backfill, identity, continuity, Test-session semantic retrieval,
  15-tool acceptance, and controlled restart gates with aggregate-only evidence.

## Changes

- #332 — privacy implementation on the v0.23.0 maintenance line.
- #333 and #338 — exact main forward-port plus the reviewed truncated-key delta.
- #339 — immutable `v0.23.1-rc1` release preparation.
- Dry-run/apply reports add aggregate selected, transformed, blocked, and policy-revision
  fields without content or identifiers.

## Not included

- #334 trajectory cloud privacy, #335 prescreen identity composition, #336 rerank payload
  privacy, and #337 remote Ollama locality are tracked follow-ups. Those features remain off
  or outside Eva's v0.23.1 configuration.
- Reranking, binary prescreen/int8, proactive recall, V4 features, raw chunk embeddings, and
  live local-model selection remain disabled for Eva.

## Contributors

- Review signal: independent blind Codex privacy review, evaos-code-review-bot,
  chatgpt-codex-connector, CodeRabbit, GitHub Actions, CodeQL, and Socket Security.

Proof boundary: the release is byte-identical to the accepted RC runtime. Publication alone
does not prove installation, runtime identity, fleet, customer, or Teams readiness.
